  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  As the State of Emergency has ended, the City Council can continue to hold virtual
  meetings without providing notice of the City Council’s teleconference location if the City
  Council makes the following two findings: (1) State or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-1 9; and
  (2) The City Council reconsiders the circumstances of the state of the emergency and
  danger presented by COVID-19; Having made the findings, the City Council can continue
  every 30 days to authorize meetings under AB 261 to protect the health or safety of
  attendees.
  Recommended Action

GENERAL BUSINESS

4.  City of Avalon General Municipal Election March 5, 2024
  —

  The City will hold its regular General Municipal Election on Tuesday, March 5, 2024 to
  elect a Mayor, two members of the City Council, a Treasurer, as well as any measures
  placed on the ballot. The City is required to adopt three resolutions, one officially calling
  for the election, one requesting the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors provide
  election services, and a resolution setting guidelines for the cost of candidate statements.
  Recommended Action
  (1) Choose among listed options regarding regulations for candidate statements:
  Statement to be limited to 200 or 400 words; Printing cost of statement in physical voter
  pamphlet and/or on the County Elections Official website; Translation cost of candidate
  statement in voter pamphlet and/or on the County Elections Official website. (2) Adopt
  Election Resolutions a.) Calling the Election, b.) Requesting the Los Angeles County
  —

  Board of Supervisors to provide election services, and c.) Adopting regulations for
  candidate statement. (3) Direct the City Clerk to publish the Notice of Election.

5.  Process in the Event of a Tie Vote at the March 5, 2023 Avalon Municipal Election
  Elections Code §15651 provides that unless the City Council adopts a resolution
  providing for a Special Runoff Election in the event of a tie vote, then tie votes are to be
  decided by the election board (the City Clerk and two designees) by lot (such as the flip
  of a coin). If the City Council decides to conduct a Special Runoff Election, it must decide
  whether this decision applies to only this election or to future elections until the City
  Council decides otherwise.
  Recommended Action
  (1) Determine appropriate action to take in case of a tie vote in the Avalon Municipal
  Election on March 5, 2024. The City Council may either: a) Adopt resolution providing for
  a Special Runoff Election in the event of a tie vote, orb) Do not adopt resolution and allow
  tie to be decided by lot. (2) Determine if the selected method should apply specifically to
  this election only, or to all subsequent elections until the City Council determines
  otherwise.

6.  Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant SDW 352 Screw Press Replacement Equipment
  Procurement
  The City’s wastewater treatment plant operator, PERC Water Corporation, is completing
  major infrastructure repairs throughout the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP).
  These repairs include establishment of redundant operational systems that will allow for
  occasional mechanical failures without creating any interruptions in system operations.

  Recommended Action
  (1) Make the affirmative finding that CCI Chemical Corporation is a sole source provider
  of a SDW 352 Screw Press as defined by the Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4111(b);
  and (2) Authorize the procurement of supplies, equipment and services for the
  replacement of the Avalon WWTP SOW 352 Screw Press Replacement for a not to
  exceed cost of $150000.00.

7.  Transit Request for Proposals
  City Staff has developed a request for proposals from qualified firms/operators to provide
  public transportation services within an approximate 1 square mile area of Avalon. The
  goal of the operation is to improve transportation and wayfinding for Avalon’s
  approximately 1 million annual visitors and its 3,500 year round residents, as well as
  alleviate congestion and demand for on street parking in Avalon’s “downtown” area.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to develop and solicit a request for proposals
  from qualified firms to provide public transportation services within the City of Avalon.

8.  Consideration to Award Contract Phase 2 Community ADA Ramp Project
  —

  In September 2023, City Staff released a Notice Inviting Bids for a Phase 2 Community
  ADA Ramp Project, funded through the Community Development Block Grant federal
  program. The scope of the project is to construct ADA compliant curb ramps at various
  locations throughout the City. The bid was to include six ramps. Four additional ramps
  were to be priced on the bid sheet as add bid items. Construction on the project may be
  completed by December 2023.
  Recommended Action
  (1) Award contract to the lowest responsible bidder for the Phase 2 Community ADA
  Ramp Project, (2) Approve the project plans, and (3) Authorize Staff to negotiate and
  execute a contract with Jordahl Construction Inc for a not to exceed sum of $218,264. (4)
  Amend the Fiscal Year 2023-24 Budget to allocate an additional $18,264 within account
  number 11930-6687, Project #180006.

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Reconsider the circumstances of COVID-1 9 state of emergency
proclaimed by the Governor and COVID-19’s continued impact and determine that state or local
officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection
with COVID-19, and as such, that continuing to utilize the protections of Assembly Bill 361 will
protect the health and safely of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. AB 361 provides an exception to these procedures in
order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including the COVID-19
pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EQ N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

Specific Findings Required underAB 361

As the State of Emergency has ended, the City Council can continue to hold virtual meetings
without providing notice of the City Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes
the following two findings:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; and

  2. The City Council reconsiders the circumstances of the state of the emergency and danger
  presented by CDVI D-19;

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S):
1) Choose among listed options regarding regulations for candidate statements:
  • Candidate statement to be limited to 200 or 400 words.
  • Printing cost of statement in physical voter pamphlet and/or on the County
  Elections Official website. (Usually paid by the candidate)
  • Translation cost of candidate statement in voter pamphlet and/or on the County
  Elections Official website. (Usually paid by the candidate)

2) Adopt Election Resolutions:
  • Resolution calling the Election.
  • Resolution requesting the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors to provide
  election services.
  • Resolution adopting regulations for candidate statement.

3) Direct the City Clerk to publish the Notice of Election.

REPORT SUMMARY; The City of Avalon will hold its regular General Municipal Election
on Tuesday, March 5, 2024 to elect a Mayor for the full term of two (2) years, two (2)
members of the City Council for the full term of four (4) years, and a Treasurer for the full
term of four (4) years, as well as any measures placed on the ballot.

The City is required to adopt three resolutions:
  1. A resolution officially calling for the election on March 5, 2024;
  2. A resolution requesting the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors provide
  election services; and
  3. A resolution setting regulations for candidate statements  —  including maximum
  word count, publication locations, and cost.

In 2022, Los Angeles County conducted a pilot program offering Online Candidate
Statement Service. The County felt the Online Candidate Statement Service was
successful and is making the offering available for cities and schools to utilize for the
March 5, 2024 Presidential Primary Election.
 Jurisdictions now have the option to aHow candidates to have statements posted on the
Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk’s website at lavote.gov without being printed in the
Official Sample Ballot Booklet. The cost for candidate statements only published online
is $279.60.

However, Los Angeles County is offering complimentary online publication of candidate
statements when a candidate opts to have their statement included in the Official Sample
Ballot Booklet. Due to Avalons small voter registry, printing a candidate statement in the
Official Ballot Booklet costs $200.

The City Council. by resolution, may authorize an option for Online Candidate Statements
in lieu of a printed statement, or may authorize the publication of both.

The City Council must decide whether candidates or the City will pay for the translation
and/or publication of the candidate statements, if the statements will appear online only,
or both online and within the Official Sample Ballot Booklet, as well as determine the
maximum length of candidate statements.

City Staff recommend adopting a resolution authorizing an option for Online Candidate
Statements as well as printed in the Official Ballot Booklet, requiring candidates to pay
for the translation and publication of the candidate’s statements, and limiting statements
to 200 words.

Los Angeles County is $17,000.00 at minimum, not including legal costs associated with
development of measures. There is $25,000 for election expenses included in FY 2023-
2024 Budget Fund 101-25-3515.

SUBJECT:  Avalon Wastewater Treatment Plant SDW 352 Screw Press

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Make the affirmative finding that CCI Chemical Corporation is
a sole source provider of a SDW 352 Screw Press as defined by the Avalon Municipal Code
Section 3-4111(b); and 2. Authorize the procurement of supplies, equipment and services for
the replacement of the Avalon WWTP SDW 352 Screw Press Replacement for a not to exceed
cost of $150,000.00.

REPORT SUMMARY:  The City’s wastewater treatment plant operator, PERC Water
Corporation (PERC), is completing major infrastructure repairs throughout the City’s Waste
Water Treatment Plant (WWTP). These repairs include establishment of redundant operational
systems that will allow for occasional mechanical failures without creating any interruptions in
system operations.

At this time, there is no screw press in operations at the WWTP. The processing of solids within
the plant is managed through the operation of a centrifuge system. Due to the high level of
salinity within the waste product (due to the usage of saltwater toilets), the waste material is
treated with additive chemicals as well as a high volume of potable water. Installation of a screw
press system will allow for the centrifuge to work as a secondary redundancy system.

Utilizing a screw press to treat solids within the WWTP will alleviate the usage of some chemicals
as well as reduce the amount of potable water necessary to break down the materials.
Additionally this technology, and overall maintenance of this system, can be performed by
current plant personnel and will not require specialized contractors/vendors.

City Staff met to see a demonstration of a screw press system in Vernon, California. Staff were
impressed by the systems efficiency and arranged for a smaller level system to be implemented
locally for a trial period. During the trial period, City and PERC Staff were impressed with overall
operations.

City Staff worked with PERO to identify CCI Chemical Corporation as a potential vendor for the
SDW 352 Screw Press System. CCI Chemical Corporation confirmed that their firm is the sole
manufacturer of the SDW 352 Screw Press System. As such, the City’s procurement policy
provides for a sole source acquisition under AMC Section 3-4111 Exceptions from Bidding and
  -

SUBJECT:  Transit Request for Proposals

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager or his designee to develop and
solicit a request for proposals from qualified firms to provide public transportation services within
the City of Avalon.

REPORT SUMMARY: During the February 21, 2023 regular City Council Meeting, the City
Council directed the City Manager to extend the contract with Transportation Concepts (TC), the
Citys contracted public transit provider, for a one-year term to allow Staff time to determine next
steps for the City’s public transportation program. The contract with TC will expire on March 31,
2024.

City Staff has developed a request for proposals from qualified firms/operators to provide public
transportation services within an approximate 1 square mile area of Avalon. The goal of the
operation is to improve transportation and wayfinding for Avalon’s approximately 1 million annual
visitors and its 3,500 year round residents, as wefl as alleviate congestion and demand for on
street parking in Avalon’s ‘downtown” area.

The City annually applies for Proposition A (Prop A) Incentive Funds through the Los Angeles
County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro). The City has received $1,000,000 in Prop
A funds annually over the last several fiscal years with $700,000 earmarked for the commuter
subsidy program, and $300,000 earmarked for the City’s land transit system. In addition to these
annual funds, the City received an additional $586,412 in ARPA Act equivalent Program Funds
through Prop A to support transit programs impacted by the COVID-19 Pandemic. On May 16,
2023, the City Council authorized spending the extra sums to offer a one-time increase to the
commuter subsidy as well as add additional funding to support land transit improvements.

City Staff determined the best use of the additional land transit funding would be to invest in the
transit fleet. On June 27, 2023 the City Council authorized the purchase of five (5) E6 GEM LSV
vehicles, charging infrastructure and digital sign boards to support the development of a micro
transit program. On September 5, 2023, the City Council authorized the purchase of one (1)
2022 Ford E-Transit 350 (12 passenger) electric van, and one (1) 2022 Ford E-Transit 350 (7+1
passenger) electric van.

The new fleet is scheduled to be on island by early 2024. The City will provide overnight parking
and charging facilities for these vehicles.
 The City is asking prospective bidders to develop a micro-transit program to include an on
demand point-to-point, fixed route and DAR transit offerings. The goal is for all offerings to be
available to the public for little to no charge. At minimum, the City is requiring the on demand
point-to-point system and DAR services be available seven (7) days a week with fixed route
supplementing operations on busy, high-passenger days.

The City’s annual transit contract is budgeted at $750,000. The potential bidder may develop
alternative revenue streams, including but not limited to advertising within the vehicles,
sponsorships for extended hours of service, etc.

The prospective operator will be required to oversee all areas of day-to-day operations, fleet and
facility management/maintenance as well as meet the reporting requirements established by
Metro and the City.
